title: I take the last train home every night. Tonight the conductor punched my ticket for a stop that isn't on the map.
transcript:
I take the last train home every night. Tonight the conductor punched my ticket for a stop that isn't on the map. I've ridden the eleven forty home for three years. Same seat, same tired faces, same eight stops.

Tonight the conductor was someone new. Tall, gloves on, a uniform a little too big. He took my ticket, looked at it for a long time, and punched a hole in it with a soft click.

When I looked down, the stop printed under the hole said Hollow Street. There is no Hollow Street on my line. I checked the map above the door twice.

At my usual stop, the doors didn't open. The train just kept rolling, and the lights outside got farther and farther apart.

I looked around for help. The other passengers were still there, but none of them were moving. Every one of them was holding a ticket with a hole punched through the same word.

The speaker crackled. A calm voice said, "Next stop, Hollow Street. Please have your ticket ready."

I tore mine up and threw the pieces under the seat. The conductor came back down the aisle, slowly, checking each face.

He stopped at me and held out his gloved hand.

In his palm was my ticket. Whole again.

"This is you," he said.
